The Public Order Act is a set of offences prohibited by law in the UK. The offences mostly revolve around public "gatherings" such as protests and riots, but it also outlaws groups from replacing the functions of the military or the police, and the equipping or training of persons intended for that purpose. It also prohibits the use of force in promoting any political object. Essentially, the law bans paramilitary groups from operating within the UK, and it was used extensively against the IRA in the 70s.

Today, the UK parliament amended the act to include the following:

"Any organisation, association or group of people residing in the UK, or areas falling under UK jurisdiction, is prohibited from being involved in the equipping, training, hiring or administration of a paramilitary group, whether it operates within UK borders or abroad. Any groups wishing to do so must have permission from the UK government.

A paramilitary group is defined as an organisation or group of people, the structure of which is similar to that of the national armed forces, or an armed group of people, the function of which is to use force for political or monetary gain."

Anyone in the UK who comes under this new amendment will have 30 days to apply for a permit to operate. If they fail to apply and do not cease their operations, they will be prosecuted.

----------

Since the UK is no longer a part of the EU, restrictions previously enforced by EU courts must be written into UK law.
